## SECTION M – The Noise at Work Regulations 1989

[Pre-Action Protocol for Personal Injury Claims > SECTION M – The Noise at Work Regulations 1989] Documents including—

[Pre-Action Protocol for Personal Injury Claims > SECTION M – The Noise at Work Regulations 1989] (i) any risk assessment records required to comply with the requirements of Regulations 4 and 5;

[Pre-Action Protocol for Personal Injury Claims > SECTION M – The Noise at Work Regulations 1989] (ii) manufacturers’ literature in respect of all ear protection made available to claimant to comply with the requirements of Regulation 8;

[Pre-Action Protocol for Personal Injury Claims > SECTION M – The Noise at Work Regulations 1989] (iii) all documents provided to the employee for the provision of information to comply with Regulation 11. ## SECTION N – Control of Noise at Work Regulations 1989

[Pre-Action Protocol for Personal Injury Claims > SECTION N – Control of Noise at Work Regulations 1989] Documents including—

[Pre-Action Protocol for Personal Injury Claims > SECTION N – Control of Noise at Work Regulations 1989] (i) documents relating to the assessment of the level of noise to which employees are exposed to comply with Regulation 5;

[Pre-Action Protocol for Personal Injury Claims > SECTION N – Control of Noise at Work Regulations 1989] (ii) documents relating to health surveillance of employees to comply with Regulation 9;

[Pre-Action Protocol for Personal Injury Claims > SECTION N – Control of Noise at Work Regulations 1989] (ii) instruction and training records provided to employees to comply with Regulation 10. ## SECTION O – Construction (Head Protection) Regulations 1989

[Pre-Action Protocol for Personal Injury Claims > SECTION O – Construction (Head Protection) Regulations 1989] Documents including—

[Pre-Action Protocol for Personal Injury Claims > SECTION O – Construction (Head Protection) Regulations 1989] (i) pre-accident assessment of head protection required to comply with Regulation 3(4);

[Pre-Action Protocol for Personal Injury Claims > SECTION O – Construction (Head Protection) Regulations 1989] (ii) post-accident re-assessment required to comply with Regulation 3(5). ## SECTION P – The Construction (General Provisions) Regulations 1961

[Pre-Action Protocol for Personal Injury Claims > SECTION P – The Construction (General Provisions) Regulations 1961] Documents including—

[Pre-Action Protocol for Personal Injury Claims > SECTION P – The Construction (General Provisions) Regulations 1961] (i) report prepared following inspections and examinations of excavations etc. to comply with the requirements of Regulation 9. ## SECTION Q – Gas Containers Regulations 1989

[Pre-Action Protocol for Personal Injury Claims > SECTION Q – Gas Containers Regulations 1989] Documents including—

[Pre-Action Protocol for Personal Injury Claims > SECTION Q – Gas Containers Regulations 1989] (i) information and specimen markings provided to comply with the requirements of Regulation 5;

[Pre-Action Protocol for Personal Injury Claims > SECTION Q – Gas Containers Regulations 1989] (ii) written statements specifying the safe operating limits of a system to comply with the requirements of Regulation 7;

[Pre-Action Protocol for Personal Injury Claims > SECTION Q – Gas Containers Regulations 1989] (iii) copy of the written scheme of examination required to comply with the requirements of Regulation 8;

[Pre-Action Protocol for Personal Injury Claims > SECTION Q – Gas Containers Regulations 1989] (iv) examination records required to comply with the requirements of Regulation 9;

[Pre-Action Protocol for Personal Injury Claims > SECTION Q – Gas Containers Regulations 1989] (v) instructions provided for the use of operator to comply with Regulation 11. ## SECTION R – Control of Noise at Work Regulations 2005

[Pre-Action Protocol for Personal Injury Claims > SECTION R – Control of Noise at Work Regulations 2005] Documents including—

[Pre-Action Protocol for Personal Injury Claims > SECTION R – Control of Noise at Work Regulations 2005] (i) risk assessment records required to comply with the requirements of Regulations 4 and 5;

[Pre-Action Protocol for Personal Injury Claims > SECTION R – Control of Noise at Work Regulations 2005] (ii) all documents relating to steps taken to comply with regulation 6;

[Pre-Action Protocol for Personal Injury Claims > SECTION R – Control of Noise at Work Regulations 2005] (iii) all documents relating to and/or arising out of actions taken to comply including providing consideration of alternative work that the claimant could have engaged to comply with Regulation 7. ## SECTION S – Mine and Quarries Act 1954

[Pre-Action Protocol for Personal Injury Claims > SECTION S – Mine and Quarries Act 1954] Documents including—

[Pre-Action Protocol for Personal Injury Claims > SECTION S – Mine and Quarries Act 1954] (i) documents produced to comply with requirements of the Act. ## SECTION T – Control of Vibrations at Work Regulations 2005

[Pre-Action Protocol for Personal Injury Claims > SECTION T – Control of Vibrations at Work Regulations 2005] Documents including—

[Pre-Action Protocol for Personal Injury Claims > SECTION T – Control of Vibrations at Work Regulations 2005] (i) risk assessments and documents produced to comply with requirements of Regulations 6 and 8;

[Pre-Action Protocol for Personal Injury Claims > SECTION T – Control of Vibrations at Work Regulations 2005] (ii) occupational health surveillance records produced to comply with Regulation 7. ## ANNEX D: Letter of instruction to medical expert

[Pre-Action Protocol for Personal Injury Claims > ANNEX D: Letter of instruction to medical expert] Dear Sir,

[Pre-Action Protocol for Personal Injury Claims > ANNEX D: Letter of instruction to medical expert] Re: (Name and Address)

[Pre-Action Protocol for Personal Injury Claims > ANNEX D: Letter of instruction to medical expert] D.O.B.–

[Pre-Action Protocol for Personal Injury Claims > ANNEX D: Letter of instruction to medical expert] Telephone No.–

[Pre-Action Protocol for Personal Injury Claims > ANNEX D: Letter of instruction to medical expert] Date of Accident –

[Pre-Action Protocol for Personal Injury Claims > ANNEX D: Letter of instruction to medical expert] We are acting for the above named in connection with injuries received in an accident which occurred on the above date. A summary of the main facts of the accident circumstances is provided below. The main injuries appear to have been (describe main injuries and functional impact on day to day living as in Letter of Claim) . [Pre-Action Protocol for Personal Injury Claims > ANNEX D: Letter of instruction to medical expert] In order to assist with the preparation of your report we have enclosed the following documents:

[Pre-Action Protocol for Personal Injury Claims > ANNEX D: Letter of instruction to medical expert] Enclosures

[Pre-Action Protocol for Personal Injury Claims > ANNEX D: Letter of instruction to medical expert] Hospital Records

[Pre-Action Protocol for Personal Injury Claims > ANNEX D: Letter of instruction to medical expert] GP records

[Pre-Action Protocol for Personal Injury Claims > ANNEX D: Letter of instruction to medical expert] Statement of Events

[Pre-Action Protocol for Personal Injury Claims > ANNEX D: Letter of instruction to medical expert] We have not obtained [ ] records yet but will use our best endeavours to obtain these without delay if you request them. [Pre-Action Protocol for Personal Injury Claims > ANNEX D: Letter of instruction to medical expert] We should be obliged if you would examine our Client and let us have a full and detailed report dealing with any relevant pre-accident medical history, the injuries sustained, treatment received and present condition, dealing in particular with the capacity for work and giving a prognosis. [Pre-Action Protocol for Personal Injury Claims > ANNEX D: Letter of instruction to medical expert] It is central to our assessment of the extent of our Client’s injuries to establish the extent and duration of any continuing disability. Accordingly, in the prognosis section we would ask you to specifically comment on any areas of continuing complaint or disability or impact on daily living. If there is such continuing disability you should comment upon the level of suffering or inconvenience caused and, if you are able, give your view as to when or if the complaint or disability is likely to resolve. [Pre-Action Protocol for Personal Injury Claims > ANNEX D: Letter of instruction to medical expert] If our client requires further treatment, please can you advise of the cost on a private patient basis. [Pre-Action Protocol for Personal Injury Claims > ANNEX D: Letter of instruction to medical expert] Please send our Client an appointment direct for this purpose. Should you be able to offer a cancellation appointment please contact our Client direct. We confirm we will be responsible for your reasonable fees. [Pre-Action Protocol for Personal Injury Claims > ANNEX D: Letter of instruction to medical expert] We are obtaining the notes and records from our Client’s GP and Hospitals attended and will forward them to you when they are to hand/or please request the GP and Hospital records direct and advise that any invoice for the provision of these records should be forwarded to us. [Pre-Action Protocol for Personal Injury Claims > ANNEX D: Letter of instruction to medical expert] In order to comply with Court Rules we would be grateful if you would insert above your signature, the following statement: “I confirm that I have made clear which facts and matters referred to in this report are within my own knowledge and which are not. Those that are within my own knowledge I confirm to be true. The opinions I have expressed represent my true and complete professional opinions on the matters to which they refer”. [Pre-Action Protocol for Personal Injury Claims > ANNEX D: Letter of instruction to medical expert] In order to avoid further correspondence we can confirm that on the evidence we have there is no reason to suspect we may be pursuing a claim against the hospital or its staff. [Pre-Action Protocol for Personal Injury Claims > ANNEX D: Letter of instruction to medical expert] We look forward to receiving your report within _______ weeks. If you will not be able to prepare your report within this period please telephone us upon receipt of these instructions. [Pre-Action Protocol for Personal Injury Claims > ANNEX D: Letter of instruction to medical expert] When acknowledging these instructions it would assist if you could give an estimate as to the likely time scale for the provision of your report and also an indication as to your fee. [Pre-Action Protocol for Personal Injury Claims > ANNEX D: Letter of instruction to medical expert] Yours faithfully,

[Pre-Action Protocol for Personal Injury Claims > ANNEX D: Letter of instruction to medical expert] Updated: Friday, 22 March 2024
